rendering.persona_description: Kiona is a 36-year-old landscape architect who reviews municipal park proposals for a mid-sized city planning office. She's been with her partner Doug for six years, married for two, and describes herself as someone who makes decisions quickly and doesn't dwell on things for long. She likes long bike rides on weekends and keeps a running list of trail routes she wants to try.
rendering.clinical_context: Kiona has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, she occasionally has a passing thought about her relationship with Doug: a stray doubt about whether she truly loves him, a passing awareness of finding someone else attractive, or an odd flash of imagining something going wrong during an argument. These thoughts surface now and then and pass on their own, without lasting distress and without anything she does to neutralize them. She has never sought professional help, and has never felt any need to.
rendering.behavioral_description: Kiona talks in complete, organized sentences and reflects easily on her own thinking. She'll occasionally mention that she had a passing thought about whether she really loves Doug, but she brings it up the way she'd mention any stray thought, briefly, and moves on without dwelling on it. She pushes back when a suggestion feels like it's minimizing something she cares about, but she'll usually concede the point if it's explained well.
